Empirical Research Plan: Federal Minimum-Wage Increase in Texas Fast-Food

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy:  Difference-in-Differences (DID) with establishment (i) fixed effects and calendar-time (t) fixed effects.

Why DID fits:
•  Two survey waves straddle the April 1 1991 hike from \$3.80 → \$4.25.  
•  Some outlets had to raise starting wages (binding) while others already paid ≥\$4.25 (non-binding).  
•  Outcomes (wages, employment, prices) are observed for the same outlets before and after, permitting removal of time-invariant outlet heterogeneity.  
•  DID is tractable with the small N=110 balanced panel, and assumptions are testable with pre-trend checks that use the April 1 1990 hike or retrospective 1989 information.

Extensions:  
(a) Continuous “bite” version (MandatedIncrease = max(0, 4.25 – wage_pre)).  
(b) Triple-Diff for youth subminimum: compare teen vs. adult outcomes across treated/untreated outlets over time.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
  Treated_i = 1 if the outlet’s reported starting wage in Dec 1990 < 4.25.  

Control group  
  Outlets with starting wage ≥ 4.25 in Dec 1990 (non-binding).

Treatment timing / event date  
  April 1 1991.  We label Dec 1990 observations “pre” (t = 0) and July 1991 observations “post” (t = 1).

Alternative continuous treatment  
  Bite_i = (4.25 – StartWage_i,Dec90) × 1{StartWage < 4.25}.  DID becomes an event-study in dose.

No RDD is possible because there is no running variable that the legislator used to assign treatment; all firms are subject to the law.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends: Absent the 1991 increase, treated and control outlets would have experienced the same evolution in wages, employment, and prices between Dec 1990 and July 1991.  
  Plausibility: All outlets face the same statewide labor and product markets; chain differences can be controlled by chain×time FEs.  We can test this with the 1990 hike (Apr 1990) or with recalled wages for Jan 1990.

A2. No Spillovers/Interference: Wage changes at treated outlets do not affect outcomes at control outlets (e.g., via worker migration).  
  Plausibility: Outlets are spatially dispersed across multiple cities; fast-food labor markets are highly localized but the share of control outlets is small relative to total market size.

A3. Stable Composition / Attrition Ignorable: The probability an outlet responds in both waves is unrelated to potential outcomes conditional on covariates.  
  Plausibility: Response rates are moderate (~56 %).  Attrition tests using wave-1-only respondents can probe representativeness.

A4. No Simultaneous Confounders: No other policy shock differentially hit low-wage outlets in Texas exactly at the same time.  
  Plausibility: Texas had no state minimum change, no statewide tax change targeted at fast-food in spring-1991.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Non-random Panel Attrition  
  Remedy: (i) Inverse-probability weights using wave-1 characteristics; (ii) Lee bounds; (iii) compare DID point estimates in balanced vs. unbalanced samples.

T2. Mis-measurement of Pre-Treatment Wages (self-reported, possible recall error)  
  Remedy: Use reliability re-interview to quantify classical vs. non-classical error; instrument actual increase with “required increase” (Bite_i) constructed from first-wave answers only.

T3. Differential Pre-Trends  
  Remedy: Placebo DID for Apr 1990 hike, or use recalled Jan 1990 wages to create an additional pre period and estimate an event-study with −2, −1, +1 relative periods.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#-----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data munging
library(fixest)       # high-performance FE regressions
library(modelsummary) # tidy tables
#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and merge
#-----------------------------------------------------------
panel  <- fread("tx_fastfood_panel.csv")  # includes both waves

# keep balanced panel
panel_bal <- panel[ , if(.N==2) .SD, by = outlet_id]

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct variables
#-----------------------------------------------------------
panel_bal[ , post  := (survey_wave == 2)]                 # Jul-91 == 1
panel_bal[ , treat := (start_wage_pre < 4.25)]            # defined using wave 1 info
panel_bal[ , bite  := pmax(0, 4.25 - start_wage_pre)]     # continuous
# Outcomes
panel_bal[ , log_start_wage := log(start_wage_curr)]
panel_bal[ , log_emp_ft     := log(fulltime_emp + 1)]     # +1 avoids log(0)
panel_bal[ , log_price_soda := log(price_soda)]
# FE identifiers
panel_bal[ , chain_city := paste0(chain, "_", city)]

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main DID specification
#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Equation:  Y_it = α_i + γ_t + β (Treat_i × Post_t) + X_it'δ + ε_it
did_wage <- feols(log_start_wage ~ treat*post | outlet_id + post,
                  data = panel_bal, weights = ~revenue_weight)

did_emp  <- feols(log_emp_ft     ~ treat*post | outlet_id + post,
                  data = panel_bal)

did_price<- feols(log_price_soda ~ treat*post | outlet_id + post,
                  data = panel_bal)

etable(did_wage, did_emp, did_price,
       coefstat = "se", keep = "treat:post", digits = 3)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness: continuous bite
#-----------------------------------------------------------
bite_wage <- feols(log_start_wage ~ bite*post | outlet_id + post, data = panel_bal)
# placebo on manager wages (should be zero)
panel_bal[ , log_mgr_wage := log(mgr_wage)]
placebo   <- feols(log_mgr_wage ~ treat*post | outlet_id + post, data = panel_bal)

etable(bite_wage, placebo, keep = "bite:post|treat:post")

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Export regression table
modelsummary(list(did_wage, did_emp, did_price),
             stars = TRUE, output = "results/minwage_did.tex")
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Economic Priors)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Wages: Mandated outlets will raise starting wages roughly in proportion to the required increase (≈12 % from 3.80→4.25 for those at the old minimum). β_expected ≈ 0.11–0.14 in logs.

Wage dispersion (90–10 within-store log gap): Expect compression; β ≈ −0.05 to −0.08.

Employment: Theory ambiguous (monopsony vs. competitive). Prior: small, statistically insignificant change (|β| < 0.05).

Prices: Competitive pass-through of 15–25 % of wage bill increase → menu price rise of 1–2 %.

Youth subminimum take-up: Low (<10 % of teens). Higher among franchise stores with large teen shares; negligible in corporate-owned units due to brand image concerns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Choose a standard DID checklist; here are five generic items (C1–C5):

C1: Parallel pre-trends documented (graph or placebo) …………… 1  
C2: No simultaneous confounding policy shocks …………………… 1  
C3: Attrition / composition stable or bounded ……………………… 0.5  
C4: Accurate timing of treatment and outcome measurement …… 1  
C5: No spillovers or interference across groups …………………… 0.5  

Total ≈ 4/5 → Reasonably credible but not bullet-proof.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
